codeReview.summary: Fail. The commit adds the requested discovery/spec-reader commands and `get-spec-full` preserves the enterprise auth/confirm safeguards required by VAL-APPS-002, but `apps global-status` does not keep its default `includeExpired=false` filter in JSON output, so VAL-APPS-001 is incomplete.

issues.description: `handleAppsGlobalStatus` expands `resourcePayload.computed ?? resourcePayload.apps` directly into `items`, so `flux apps global-status --json` can return expired apps even when `--include-expired` is omitted (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:5633-5656`). The MCP tool filters preview rows with `const filtered = includeExpired ? computed : computed.filter((x) => x.expired !== true);` but stores the full computed set in the resource payload (`flux-mcp/src/index.ts:6934-6999`). The added tests only cover a non-expired fixture (`fluxos-cli/test/apps-discovery-specs.test.ts:673-685`), so this selector drift is not caught.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The shared docs do not call out that table-backed MCP resources may persist the unfiltered computed dataset rather than the filtered preview rows. CLI adapters need to reapply user-facing filters when turning those resources back into JSON.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `flux-mcp/src/index.ts:6934-6999` filters rows for display but stores `computed` in the resource payload; `fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:5633-5656` consumes that payload directly and drops the `includeExpired=false` selector.
